summary: The configuration-index finding is settled and witnessed, so this turn went back to the second open A2 question: whether a duty the public API has already accepted still has a completion path when authority is lost by Shutdown rather than by stepping down. Source reading gives a three-part mechanism that is independently checkable: the caller's timeout is used only in the select that enqueues the future into applyCh (api.go:829-851, 859-877), so it never bounds completion; the returned logFuture carries no ShutdownCh, so deferError.Error() waits on the internal error channel alone (future.go:113-118) while only restore and snapshot-internal futures are wired to shutdownCh (raft.go:1169, 1914, snapshot.go:152); and Shutdown() closes shutdownCh and sets state Shutdown without draining applyCh (api.go:1012-1025), leaving runLeader's defer to cover only futures already on leaderState.inflight (raft.go:502-560). BatchApplyCh is the documented option that separates acceptance from consumption, and its own comment already concedes it breaks the timeout guarantee on Apply (config.go:169-174); the repository's own test file notes the same stuck-future class at raft_test.go:40-42. I did not assert the defect from reading: this turn submits the experiment plus the two supporting behaviors and the necessary gap, with the interpretation to follow from the receipt. The harness occupies the main loop through the public Restore path with a caller-supplied reader that stalls on its first Read (which doubles as the freeze handshake), accepts one Barrier future through the ordinary public path so it lands in the buffered applyCh, calls Shutdown(), and emits one CA_EVENT line recording the completion result, the remaining queue depth and capacity, the node state at acceptance and after shutdown, plus a control Barrier on the undisturbed leader to show the same call does complete when a producer exists. Both files validate; the experiment is queued for clean-copy execution.
